    def dfun(self, state_variables, coupling, local_coupling=0):

        # shape (n_sv, n_modes)
        xi = state_variables[0, :]
        eta = state_variables[1, :]
        alpha = state_variables[2, :]
        beta = state_variables[3, :]

        tau = self.tau
        a = self.a
        b = self.b
        K11 = self.K11
        K12 = self.K12
        K21 = self.K21

        # Coupling Terms (from coupling array)
        c_glob = coupling[0, :]

        # Derived Variables
        self.Aik = Aik = 0.500000000000000
        self.Bik = Bik = 0.500000000000000
        self.Cik = Cik = 0.500000000000000
        self.e_i = e_i = 1.00000000000000
        self.f_i = f_i = 1.00000000000000
        self.IE_i = IE_i = 0.0
        self.II_i = II_i = 0.0
        self.m_i = m_i = a
        self.n_i = n_i = a

        # Time Derivatives
        # Broadcast every derivative to a common per-node shape so constant
        # (state-independent) derivatives — e.g. ``duA/dt = cA`` — stack into a
        # homogeneous array alongside node-shaped ones, matching TVB's own
        # ``numpy.full_like`` handling of constant drifts.
        _derivs = np.broadcast_arrays(
            np.asarray(
                K11 * (-xi + Aik * xi)
                + tau * (IE_i + c_glob + local_coupling * xi)
                + tau * (xi - eta - 1 / 3 * e_i * xi**3)
                - K12 * (-xi + Bik * alpha)
            ),  # xi
            np.asarray((m_i + xi - b * eta) / tau),  # eta
            np.asarray(
                K21 * (-alpha + Cik * xi)
                + tau * (II_i + c_glob + local_coupling * xi)
                + tau * (alpha - beta - 1 / 3 * f_i * alpha**3)
            ),  # alpha
            np.asarray((alpha + n_i - b * beta) / tau),  # beta
        )
        return np.array(_derivs)
